# Data classes and retention

Every classified column on the platform, and what happens to it ([ADR-0301](../adr/0301-data-lifecycle-privacy.md)).

This is the checklist a new service is reviewed against. A service can otherwise omit its obligations silently, and the omission surfaces on the first erasure request that needs it — which is a month before the deadline, at best.

**It is a view, not a source.** The classes come from the `pii:<class>` tags in the migrations, where the tag lives in the DDL and travels with the schema; the periods and disposals come from `tools/codegen/retention.yaml`, because how long to keep a class and whether to delete or anonymise it are decisions a column tag cannot carry. Editing this file changes nothing: add the tag, or change the policy.

## Policy per class

| Class | Retention | At the end | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `contact` | life of the account, then 30 days | delete | Email, phone, postal address. Directly identifying, so an erasure request removes it rather than anonymising it. |
| `device` | 90 days | delete | IP address, user agent, device identifier. Raw IP addresses are not stored at all (ADR-0700); what falls under this class is what survives reduction. |
| `financial` | 7 years | anonymise | Payment instrument details. The period is a bookkeeping obligation rather than a product decision, and it overrides an erasure request for the row's financial fields. |
| `free_text` | life of the account, then 30 days | delete | A field a user types into, which may hold anything. Treated at the strictest plausible class because its contents cannot be predicted. |
| `government_id` | only while a legal obligation requires it | delete | National identifier, passport, tax number. The shortest period of any class, because holding one without a live obligation is the risk. |
| `identifier` | life of the account, then 30 days | anonymise | A pseudonymous subject or account identifier. Anonymised rather than deleted because rows keyed by it — orders, charges — carry their own retention obligation that outlives the account. |
| `location` | 90 days | delete | Coordinates and precise geolocation. |
| `name` | life of the account, then 30 days | delete | A person's name. |
| `none` | n/a | n/a | Considered and carries no personal data. The tag exists so that "nobody looked" and "someone decided" are distinguishable. |
| `special_category` | only while a legal obligation requires it | delete | GDPR Art. 9 — health, biometrics, and the rest. The platform stores none today, and the class exists so that adding one is a deliberate act against a stated rule. |

## What this does not cover

Telemetry retention belongs to [ADR-0500](../adr/0500-observability.md) and backup retention to [ADR-0200](../adr/0200-cluster-topology.md). This registry owns application data, which is the part an erasure request reaches.

A column tagged `pii:none` appears here too, and that is the point: the tag distinguishes "someone considered this and it holds no personal data" from "nobody looked".
